record.paper_title: Open Problems in α Particle Condensation
record.context_brief: Experimental verification of the ¹⁶O condensate candidate
record.original_question: In ¹⁶O, is the sixth 0⁺ state at 15.1 MeV, about 700 keV above the four-α threshold, an α-particle condensate analogous to the Hoyle state, and can this be established experimentally through inelastic electromagnetic form factors and four-α coincidence measurements with invariant-mass reconstruction?

evidence.quote: Theory predicts that analogues to the Hoyle state in 12C with its three α particles condensed into a common 0S orbit also should exist around the nα threshold in heavier self conjugate nuclei [1, 2, 3, 4]. We have made a prediction that the 6-th 0+ state at 15.1 MeV in 16O should be such a state [5].

Inelastic electromagnetic form factors are very much in need. The Hoyle state has very clearly been identified from a three α coincidence measurement [7], hinting to its α-gas like structure. A 4α coincidence measurement in 16O with determination of the invariant mass, would be extremely useful.
One of the most urgent issues is to verify experimentally that in 16O indeed the 15.1 MeV state is an α particle condensate state.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the oxygen-16 nucleus, ${}^{16}\mathrm{O}$, regarded as a system of four α particles plus additional internal degrees of freedom. The four-α breakup threshold lies at about 14.4 MeV of excitation, and ${}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ possesses a sixth $0^+$ excited state at an excitation energy near 15.1 MeV (about 700 keV above the four-α threshold). 

By an "α-particle condensate state" we mean a state in which the constituent α clusters predominantly occupy the lowest ($0S$) single-particle orbital of an effective mean field, producing a dilute, weakly interacting α-gas-like structure analogous to the second $0^+$ state of ${}^{12}\mathrm{C}$ (the Hoyle state), in which three α particles are believed to condense into a common $0S$ orbit.

Question: Is the sixth $0^+$ state of ${}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ at 15.1 MeV an α-particle condensate state of four α particles in the above sense? Furthermore, can its condensate nature be established experimentally through measurements of the inelastic electromagnetic transition form factors to this state combined with four-α coincidence measurements (with full invariant-mass reconstruction of the four-α final state) in a manner analogous to how the Hoyle state in ${}^{12}\mathrm{C}$ was characterized via three-α coincidence experiments?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent experimental and theoretical work has addressed the question but not fully resolved it. An analysis of α+¹⁶O diffraction scattering found no enhanced radius for the 15.1 MeV 0⁺₆ state, contradicting the giant-radius prediction of the α-condensate model. A dedicated four-α coincidence breakup experiment via inelastic α scattering at 45 MeV reported inconclusive signatures for the 15.1 MeV state. Thus the condensate identification has not been experimentally confirmed and is in tension with some data, while the question remains under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Do analogs of the Hoyle state exist in 16O?
status_evidence.snippet: No case of a significant enhancement of the radius with respect to its ground-state value was observed, particularly for the 15.1-MeV 0⁺₆ state, for which a giant radius predicted by the alpha-particle-condensate model was not confirmed.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental radius analysis does not support the condensate prediction for the 15.1 MeV 0⁺ state in ¹⁶O.

status_evidence.title: Search for the Hoyle analogue state in ¹⁶O
status_evidence.snippet: Inelastic scattering of 45 MeV alphas with 4α breakup detected in coincidence in complete kinematics; signature of the 15.1 MeV state remains inconclusive.
status_evidence.claim: A dedicated four-α coincidence experiment did not provide a conclusive identification of the 15.1 MeV state as a Hoyle analogue.

status_evidence.title: The Hoyle Family: The Search for Alpha-Condensate States in Light Nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Review of ongoing search for α-condensate states in light nuclei including ¹⁶O.
status_evidence.claim: The identification of α-condensate states beyond the Hoyle state in ¹²C is still an open research program.
